approval.cost: No fee for client registration or API access is stated in the documentation read
approval.trigger: No review or approval step is described in the Zoho Books API documentation or the Zoho Accounts OAuth protocol documentation read: client registration in the API Console is self-serve (fill in the form, click CREATE, receive credentials), and the documented flow then allows any end user to authorize a server-based client ('intended for use by multiple Zoho accounts'). There is no documented app review, verification program, or approval gate before external users can connect, and no pre-approval user/install caps (the per-user/per-client token caps are operational limits, not approval caps). No marketplace/directory listing process for Books OAuth clients is described in the documentation read.
approval.wait: None (no review exists in the docs read)

blockers.detail: Zoho Accounts domains are per-DC (US accounts.zoho.com, EU accounts.zoho.eu, IN, AU, JP, CA, SA, UK) and the Books API base URIs are likewise per-DC. Codes and tokens are DC-bound: 'If the user account is in the EU, the generated code will also be in EU only and not in other DCs.' Your client must have Multi DC enabled (console > client > Settings > toggle DCs) to serve users outside your home DC; 'The Client ID will be common for all DCs, but the Client Secret can be either common to all the DCs or unique for each DC depending on your preference' (per-DC secrets by default). Using credentials from the wrong DC yields invalid_client.
blockers.howToClear: Route token calls by the location/accounts-server values returned at authorization, enable Multi DC, and manage per-DC secrets.
blockers.title: Data-center fragmentation

blockers.detail: 'Each time a re-consent is accepted, a new refresh token is generated. The maximum limit is 20 refresh tokens per user. If this limit is crossed, the first refresh token is automatically deleted to accommodate the latest one. This is done irrespective of whether the first refresh token is in use or not.' Related throttles: max 10 grant tokens per client ID in 10 minutes; max 10 access tokens from a refresh token in 10 minutes; max 15 active access tokens per refresh token (the 16th invalidates the oldest).
blockers.howToClear: Avoid gratuitous re-consents, reuse valid access tokens, and design re-authorization recovery for evicted refresh tokens.
blockers.title: The 20-refresh-token cap silently deletes in-use tokens

blockers.detail: 'If the access_type is not mentioned as offline, by default it will be considered as online... If the value is online, you will receive only the access token.' And getting a second refresh token later requires both parameters: 'To receive another refresh token, include access_type=offline and prompt=consent in your authorization request.' Zoho's own troubleshooting lists the missing refresh token as the most common error here.
blockers.howToClear: Always send access_type=offline (and prompt=consent when re-consenting for a new refresh token).
blockers.title: access_type defaults to online: no refresh token

flavor.recommended: A Server-based Application client in the Zoho API Console, authorized with access_type=offline
flavor.why: The object is a Client registered in the Zoho Developer Console / Zoho API Console (api-console.zoho.com); the authorization server is Zoho Accounts, not Books itself. This is ONE Zoho-wide OAuth client, not a Books-specific app object: Books is simply one service name in the shared scope system. Zoho describes Server-based Applications as 'intended for use by multiple Zoho accounts' with 'a dedicated backend server and web UI to handle the authorization process'. Books-specific scopes follow the format service_name.scope_name.operation_type (e.g. ZohoBooks.invoices.READ, ZohoBooks.contacts.CREATE) across modules including contacts, settings, estimates, invoices, customerpayments, creditnotes, projects, expenses, salesorders, purchaseorders, bills, debitnotes, vendorpayments, banking, and accountants. No API-key auth is documented for the Books API: 'The Zoho Books APIs use the Open Authorization (OAuth) 2.0 protocol for authentication.'

humanMust: Register the client in the Zoho API Console under your own Zoho account
Optionally enable Multi DC for the client (Settings tab) and manage per-DC client secrets
name: Zoho Books
nuances: Despite token_type 'Bearer' in token responses, Books API calls must use 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token}' ('Strictly follow this format'), header only: 'The access Token can be passed only in the header and cannot be passed in the request param.'

organization_id is mandatory on Books calls: a token alone is insufficient; every Books API request carries the connected organization's ID as a query parameter, and a single Zoho user can belong to multiple Books organizations, so your connection record must store which organization the grant was for.

Grant tokens: web flow code 'valid only for two minutes and is only one time usable'; Self Client grant tokens are 'valid for three minutes, by default' (extendable via a console dropdown). Access tokens are valid for one hour (expires_in 3600). Refresh tokens: 'A refresh token does not expire... until a user revokes them', but a stored refresh token may be deleted if the user revoked it under Connected Apps, if it was revoked via /oauth/v2/token/revoke, or if 'You changed your Zoho Accounts password and opted for the removal of the web sessions'.

Token endpoint mechanics: POST only (browser GET attempts produce a 'server error' deliberately, because the request carries secrets), and parameters must be sent as params/query string, NOT a JSON body (else invalid_client).

Scope discipline: tokens work 'only for the operations that are specified in the scope', scopes are displayed at consent, and an invalid/nonexistent scope yields 'Invalid OAuth scope' at authorization time; scope names must match the Books module list exactly (customerpayments and salesorders are single tokens in scope strings even where module display names differ).
prerequisites: A Zoho account for the API Console
Client Name, Homepage URL, and Authorized Redirect URLs
A DC strategy and per-connection storage for organization_id

steps.detail: api-console.zoho.com > Server-based Applications: Client Name, Homepage URL, Authorized Redirect URLs, CREATE. 'You will receive the Client ID and Client Secret.' Optionally enable Multi DC (client > Settings tab > toggle the required DCs).
steps.title: Register a Server-based client

steps.detail: GET {Accounts_URL}/oauth/v2/auth with client_id, response_type=code, redirect_uri (must match the registered one), scope (comma-separated ZohoBooks.* scopes, shown at consent), access_type=offline, and optional prompt=consent. On Accept, Zoho redirects with code plus location/accounts-server for DC routing; on Deny, 'the server will return an error'.
steps.title: Redirect the user to authorize (access_type=offline)

steps.detail: The code 'will be valid for 2 minutes'. POST {Accounts_URL}/oauth/v2/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, client_id, client_secret, redirect_uri, sent as params (not a JSON body), at the user's DC accounts URL. Response: access_token, refresh_token, api_domain, token_type Bearer, expires_in 3600.
steps.title: Exchange the code immediately (2-minute validity)

steps.detail: Call https://www.zohoapis.com/books/v3/... (or the DC api_domain) with header 'Authorization: Zoho-oauthtoken {access_token}' and ?organization_id={id} on every request. Store the refresh token, api_domain, and organization_id per connection.
steps.title: Call the Books API (Zoho-oauthtoken header + organization_id)

steps.detail: POST {Accounts_URL}/oauth/v2/token with grant_type=refresh_token, refresh_token, client_id, client_secret, at the same DC. Revoke via POST {Accounts_URL}/oauth/v2/token/revoke with token = the access or refresh token when a user disconnects.
steps.title: Refresh; revoke on disconnect

tagline: Zoho's shared OAuth client model applied to accounting: no client review, granular ZohoBooks scopes, and a mandatory organization_id on every call, with the platform's usual traps (per-data-center endpoints and secrets, a 20-refresh-token cap, and a 2-minute code).

time.active: ~5 min of console setup + ~1-2 hrs of DC-aware flow code
time.total: Same day; no approval wait exists
